title: Gambhir, Agarkar Identify Tilak Varma as Shreyas Iyer's ODI World Cup Backup
excerpt: India's selectors are grooming the T20I vice-captain as a middle-order insurance policy for the 2027 tournament in South Africa.
body:
• India's team management has identified Tilak Varma as the primary backup for Shreyas Iyer at No. 4 ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa.
  • Head coach Gautam Gambhir and captain Shubman Gill want a top-order batter who can contribute four overs of off-spin in ODIs, reducing reliance on injury-prone all-rounders.
  • Tilak's left-handed batting adds variety to a predominantly right-handed lineup, while his T20I record — 1,390 runs at 44.83 — supports his case for a 50-over role.
  • The ODI series against West Indies in September and the New Zealand tour in October will serve as trial windows, with several regulars unavailable due to the 2026 Asian Games.

Middle-Order Insurance for South Africa

India's selectors and coaching staff have zeroed in on Tilak Varma as the leading backup for Shreyas Iyer in the middle order ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup, according to a report by Arani Basu of the Times of India. The 23-year-old left-hander, currently India's T20I vice-captain, is being prepared for a dual role: a middle-order stabilizer who can also chip in with part-time off-spin.

The push comes from the top. A BCCI source told the Times of India that both head coach Gautam Gambhir and ODI captain Shubman Gill have flagged the absence of a ready-made backup in the middle order — a concern sharpened by the injury histories of Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar Reddy.

"Head coach Gautam Gambhir and captain Shubman Gill feel there isn't any backup ready for the middle order. With Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar Reddy being prone to injuries, they want someone in the top order who can at least chip in with four overs in an ODI."

— BCCI source, via Times of India

The Case for Tilak at No. 4

Iyer's credentials at No. 4 are established: 2,977 ODI runs at an average of 47, with five centuries and 23 fifties across 76 matches. He is India's ODI vice-captain under Gill. Tilak, by contrast, has played just five ODIs for 68 runs at 22.66. The statistical gap is wide, but the selectors are looking beyond the numbers.

Two factors make Tilak the logical choice. First, he is a left-hander in a top six composed almost entirely of right-handed batters. India's ODI lineup features Gill, Iyer, KL Rahul, and Virat Kohli — all right-handed. Tilak's presence disrupts bowling plans and forces field changes in a way that no other backup candidate can replicate.

Second, Tilak's off-spin has been identified as a genuine asset. The management has specifically asked him to develop his bowling, aiming to fill a gap that has long placed excessive demands on specialist bowlers. India learned this lesson at the 2023 World Cup, when Pandya injured his ankle against Bangladesh and left the team without a sixth bowling option for the remainder of the tournament.

T20I Dominance Supports the Transition

Tilak's case rests heavily on what he has already demonstrated in T20Is. His 1,390 runs at an average of 44.83 include back-to-back unbeaten centuries against South Africa in November 2024 — 107 not out and 120 not out — scored in contrasting match situations. In the 2025 Asia Cup final against Pakistan, his 69 off 53 balls was a masterclass in innings management under pressure.

The selectors have already tested the interchangeability between Tilak and Iyer. When Tilak suffered an injury during the Vijay Hazare Trophy in January 2026, Iyer was slotted directly into his T20I position. That swap worked well enough for Iyer to continue into the T20 World Cup squad and eventually be named India's T20I captain in June 2026, with Tilak as his vice-captain.

In June 2026, Tilak captained India A in the ODI tri-series in Sri Lanka, scoring 60 against Sri Lanka A while forming a 150-run partnership with Ruturaj Gaikwad after India A slipped to 16 for 2. Chief selector Ajit Agarkar had flagged Tilak's proximity to the ODI squad as early as October 2025, noting he was "very close" to breaking in.

The Ageing Core and the Fitness Question

The urgency extends beyond Iyer's backup. The BCCI source pointed to broader concerns about India's ageing squad. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli, both in their late thirties, have been dealing with recurring niggles. KL Rahul will be over 35 by the time the World Cup arrives. Ravindra Jadeja's place is no longer a certainty either.

"The team has to be prepared for conditions in South Africa. Iyer got injured in Australia, and his game against pace and bounce is untested of late. The team already has two ageing players in Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli."

— BCCI source, via Times of India

India's fielding standards have also suffered due to fitness issues, reinforcing the case for injecting younger legs into the squad. The picture will become clearer during the New Zealand tour in October, which includes all three formats. Before that, the home ODI series against West Indies starting September 27 will offer audition opportunities, with several first-choice players unavailable due to the 2026 Asian Games in Japan.

India have 24 ODIs across eight bilateral series before the World Cup. For Indian cricket fans worldwide, the question is no longer whether Tilak will get a serious ODI audition, but how quickly he can translate his T20I dominance into the 50-over game.
